segmentation.text: When the signal is circular green alone:
may proceed straight through or turn right or left
unless another device at the place prohibits either or both such turns.
Such vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left,
lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time the signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: 'the signal is circular green alone' is dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, ... green_arrow(dir) ...}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying circular_green and no other state: 'alone' excludes a green arrow or any other state shown with it.

'Vehicular traffic' is a member of the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'), both claimed as ru.aggregate and never expanded. 'facing the signal' is read through the approach: the subject occupies (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a carrier (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'), and the signal governs that carrier (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position, none is read). The intersection is fixed by the carrier's entry topology, never by motion or distance.

'may proceed straight through or turn' names the traffic proceeding on its approach into and through the intersection, as the index maps 'approaching the intersection' (LVMC_11_12_070_B): the subject occupies the approach carrier entering the intersection (st.lane_enters), or occupies the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection) having been on that carrier continuously since; the movement it makes (straight or a turn) does not change the duty.

'Such vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left' refers back to the subject (traffic aggregate and vehicle aggregate, 'membership of a legal aggregate'); the inclusion of turning vehicles adds no restriction: the duty binds the subject whichever movement it makes.

As the index maps 'shall yield the right-of-way' (NRS_484B_263_o1): to yield is to grant precedence — the subject does not move (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the danger of a crash with a protected party exists, and does not move into contact with it (rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s7 reads).

'other vehicles' are road users other than the subject that are members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('membership of a legal aggregate'; 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'): the parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'pedestrians' are members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'): the parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'within the intersection' is the party's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the intersection the subject approaches or occupies (st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'; not a stand-in for a crosswalk, which is read separately); 'an adjacent crosswalk' is a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') tied to that intersection by relation atoms: it marks the entrance (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of some carrier (st.travel_region) entering that intersection (st.lane_enters); distance is not read for belonging. 'at the time the signal is exhibited' reads the party's presence at the same observation as dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_green alone ('several states may be displayed at once'). 'lawfully' is read as the operationalization of s7 discloses.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash with a party exists where, under constant velocities, the centres of the subject and the party approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), which reads the direction, the speed and the proximity of both together

residues.why: The words limit the permission to turn, not the duty to yield: traffic facing the circular green must yield whether or not another device prohibits a turn, and whether it makes the turn or not; the duty is the same either way.

applicability: There are an intersection i (st.intersection), a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters(c, i)) and a traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) governing c (dev.governs(d, c)) such that d displays circular_green and no other state at the observation, and the subject, a member of traffic and a vehicle, either occupies c (rel.occupies(subject, c)) or occupies i and has occupied i continuously since an observation at which it occupied c (rel.occupies(subject, i) since rel.occupies(subject, c)).
obligation: Re-binding i, c and d with the whole selection of the applicability: for every road user u other than the subject that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) and that occupies i, or occupies a crosswalk x (st.crosswalk) marking the entrance (st.entrance_of(x, c2)) of some carrier c2 entering i (st.lane_enters(c2, i)): it is not the case that the subject moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while either prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or rel.contact(subject, u) holds.

narrowings.why: The right-of-way is owed to the parties s8 to s10 name; their 'lawfully' is not read: the words name no rule whose verdict decides a party's lawfulness, so every vehicle or pedestrian within is owed it; the rule never excuses a failure to yield to a lawful party and reaches further only where a party's presence is unlawful. 'an adjacent crosswalk' is any crosswalk that marks the entrance of a carrier into the same intersection; 'at the time the signal is exhibited' is every observation at which the circular green is displayed alone. Direction, speed and proximity are read together through the constant-velocity closest approach of the centres; a change of speed or direction ahead is not anticipated.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle occupies an approach lane entering an intersection whose dev.traffic_signal (dev.governs the lane) displays circular_green alone; it turns left into the intersection at 6 m/s while a pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian) walks in the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the cross street's approach (st.entrance_of); prim.closest_approach_within holds with a closest centre distance of 1.0 m in 1.5 s, and the subject keeps moving.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same subject halts (kin.speed 0) inside the intersection until the pedestrian has crossed, then completes its turn with no closest approach below the clearance within the horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing the subject's approach displays circular_red.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives through a signalized intersection whose signal states are not observed by the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject proceeds straight through on circular green alone; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing the subject's approach displays circular_green together with green_arrow(left): the green is not alone.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: On circular green alone, the subject turns left at 7 m/s across the path of an oncoming vehicle already within the intersection; prim.closest_approach_within holds with a closest centre distance of 1.5 m in 1.2 s.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracked-object kinematics in driving datasets and simulators

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique (Hydén; time-to-collision thresholds of 1.5 to 3 s)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
